$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =0.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-6{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].

"cc10999e-0e98-57c8-9318-5ca4b1f6c8ec" :question/math-academy-id "q-80323" :question/problem "Given that $\lambda =-2$ and $\lambda =-1$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -12 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$" :question/worked-solution "To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =-2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -12 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{4}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =-1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -12 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -12 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -12 & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=4{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d5476fb6-80da-5fb0-9202-81c168d50130"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id $$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =0.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]-0[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 

From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
-6{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, setting ${x}_{2}=3,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$

"cc10999e-0e98-57c8-9318-5ca4b1f6c8ec" :question/math-academy-id "q-80323" :question/problem "Given that $\lambda =-2$ and $\lambda =-1$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -12 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]$,
find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$" :question/worked-solution "To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =-2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -12 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 & 0 \\ 1 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{4}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =-1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -12 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -12 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -12 & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{3}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=4{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d5476fb6-80da-5fb0-9202-81c168d50130"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id find two linearly independent eigenvectors of $A.$" :question/worked-solution "To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each of the eigenvalues separately. 

- For $\lambda =4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain  ${x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For $\lambda =5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. 
From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, two linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix $A$ are

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$"] ["question-4056bc20-f830-546e-b11d-9973d25fccb0" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["answer-field-90ab5756-be68-58c5-811b-5048edcd87d1" :answer-field/id #uuid
